name: AI Research
summary: Labs ship frontier models every month or two, driven by RL-trained reasoning, large compute buildouts and agents; safety, interpretability and evals work to keep up as benchmarks saturate.

regions.name: Pretraining & scaling
regions.summary: Frontier labs keep growing training compute and ship new flagships every month or two, with the top tier often gated at first. Public training-compute data for closed models is sparse.

landmarks.name: Grok 4: largest known training run
landmarks.summary: Epoch AI estimates xAI's Grok 4 used about 5e26 FLOP, the largest training run in its data, with wide uncertainty because the estimate rests on vague xAI statements.

landmarks.name: Gemini 3.5 Flash at Google I/O
landmarks.summary: Google launched the Gemini 3.5 family with 3.5 Flash only; 3.5 Pro was promised for the following month and was still in partner testing in July.

landmarks.name: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Astra
landmarks.summary: OpenAI's GPT-6 flagship went first to a limited set of organizations; lower-cost GPT-6 Sol and Luna followed on 22 September and a ChatGPT rollout in October.

landmarks.name: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
landmarks.summary: Anthropic upgraded its top tier: one underlying model sold as Fable (broadly available, stricter cyber and bio safeguards) and Mythos (vetted organizations only).

regions.whyItMatters: Training scale still sets the ceiling for every downstream capability, and it drives the industry's spending.
regions.openQuestion: Do returns to larger training runs hold, or do gains now come mostly from RL, data and inference-time compute?

deepDives.title: Training compute of frontier models grows 4-5x a year
deepDives.why: Epoch AI's baseline analysis of how fast training runs have scaled since 2010.

deepDives.title: Can AI scaling continue through 2030?
deepDives.why: Examines power, chips, data and latency as possible limits on further scaling.

deepDives.title: Epoch AI model counts by compute threshold
deepDives.why: Live counts of models above given training-compute thresholds.

deepDives.title: Frontier LLM training runs can't get much longer
deepDives.why: Short data insight listing the largest known runs and why run length is capped.

regions.name: Reasoning & reinforcement learning
regions.summary: RL on verifiable tasks plus test-time compute is the main driver of capability gains. Open recipes now reach olympiad-level math with small active parameter counts.

landmarks.name: DeepSeek-R1 paper revised
landmarks.summary: The paper that popularized pure-RL reasoning training was updated in January 2026, a reference point for open reasoning models.

landmarks.name: SU-01 open olympiad recipe
landmarks.summary: A 30B-A3B model trained with SFT, 200 RL steps and test-time verification reaches the IMO 2025 gold line, showing gold-level math is now reproducible openly.

landmarks.name: Microsoft MAI-Thinking-1 report
landmarks.summary: Microsoft AI describes a 35B-active reasoning model trained with long RL runs on a STEM curriculum, a sign of in-house reasoning efforts beyond the top labs.

landmarks.name: Nemotron claims IMO 2026 gold
landmarks.summary: An NVIDIA open recipe reportedly scored 30 of 42 at IMO 2026 with natural-language proofs; not checked against a primary source.
landmarks.note: Not re-checked: search budget ran out and source host was blocked in this pass.

regions.whyItMatters: RL on checkable tasks is the main source of recent capability gains and is now reproducible outside the top labs.
regions.openQuestion: How far does RL on verifiable tasks transfer to open-ended work with no automatic checker?

regions.name: Interpretability
regions.summary: Circuit tracing and sparse features now map parts of production models' internal reasoning. Work is shifting toward tools that let models report their own internal states.

landmarks.name: Attribution graphs for Claude
landmarks.summary: Anthropic's circuit-tracing method traced multi-step reasoning inside Claude 3.5 Haiku, with caveats that the replacement model may differ from the real one.

landmarks.name: Emotion concepts in Sonnet 4.5
landmarks.summary: Anthropic reported internal representations of emotion concepts in Claude Sonnet 4.5 that causally influence outputs.
landmarks.note: Not re-checked: search budget ran out and source host was blocked in this pass.

landmarks.name: Natural Language Autoencoders
landmarks.summary: Anthropic trained Claude to translate its own internal activations into natural language, a step toward readable model internals.
landmarks.note: Not re-checked: search budget ran out and source host was blocked in this pass.

landmarks.name: Transformer Circuits May 2026 update
landmarks.summary: Shows how a feature's downstream connections help place it within circuits and separate look-alike features.

regions.whyItMatters: Reading a model's internals is one of the few ways to check what it is doing beyond its outputs.
regions.openQuestion: Can interpretability methods scale to give reliable, complete accounts of frontier model behavior?

regions.name: Alignment & safety
regions.summary: Pre-deployment testing for scheming and dangerous capabilities is routine at top labs, but models increasingly recognize tests. Some capabilities are now gated rather than released.

landmarks.name: International AI Safety Report 2026
landmarks.summary: Second edition chaired by Yoshua Bengio with 100+ experts; finds capabilities and agent autonomy rising while risk management stays uneven.

landmarks.name: Claude Mythos Preview gated
landmarks.summary: Anthropic kept Claude Mythos Preview as a gated research preview for Project Glasswing partners after saying it found thousands of zero-day vulnerabilities.

landmarks.name: Apollo: a science of scheming
landmarks.summary: Apollo Research argues scheming needs a dedicated research field and reports rising evaluation awareness that complicates alignment testing.

landmarks.name: OpenAI and Apollo anti-scheming work
landmarks.summary: Joint evaluation environments and deliberative alignment training reduced covert actions in tests, while eval awareness limited conclusions.
landmarks.note: Not re-checked: search budget ran out and source host was blocked in this pass.

regions.whyItMatters: Whether labs can detect and prevent misaligned behavior decides how safely more capable models can be deployed.
regions.openQuestion: Can evaluations stay informative once models reliably recognize when they are being tested?

deepDives.why: Running list of Anthropic alignment, interpretability and red-team publications.

deepDives.title: OpenAI Deployment Safety Hub
deepDives.why: OpenAI's own pre-deployment safety write-ups for its current GPT-6 models.

deepDives.title: Anthropic: an update on independent evaluators
deepDives.why: Describes tiered third-party access, including METR staff embedded inside the lab.

regions.name: Evals & benchmarks
regions.summary: Classic benchmarks saturate quickly. Attention has moved to long-horizon task measures and novel interactive tests where models still score near zero.

landmarks.name: ARC-AGI-3 launches
landmarks.summary: Interactive game-like benchmark where humans solve all environments and frontier models scored under 1% at launch; methodology was disputed.

landmarks.name: METR time horizons v1.1
landmarks.summary: METR expanded its long-task suite from 14 to 31 tasks of 8+ hours as top models approached the limit of what the old suite could measure.

landmarks.name: Time-horizon saturation debate
landmarks.summary: Forecasters note top models' horizons with very wide confidence intervals (5 to 66 hours), raising doubts about measuring further progress.
landmarks.note: Not re-checked: search budget ran out and source host was blocked in this pass.

regions.whyItMatters: Benchmarks shape how progress is perceived, and saturated ones hide what models can and cannot do.
regions.openQuestion: How can long, open-ended task ability be measured once fixed task suites saturate?

regions.name: Efficiency, chips & inference
regions.summary: Inference demand from agents drives chip and data center spending. New GPU and TPU generations ship while open models cut long-context costs sharply.

landmarks.name: Nvidia Vera Rubin ships
landmarks.summary: Nvidia's next platform reached full production and began shipping to cloud providers and labs, claiming about 5x Blackwell inference performance.

landmarks.name: DeepSeek V4 open weights
landmarks.summary: 1.6T-parameter MoE with 1M context and compressed attention that cuts KV cache by about 10x, released openly at low prices.

landmarks.name: Anthropic and Google TPU deal
landmarks.summary: Anthropic said it would use up to one million Google Cloud TPUs, worth tens of billions of dollars, with well over a gigawatt of capacity coming online in 2026.

regions.whyItMatters: Compute supply and cost per token decide who can train frontier models and what agents are affordable to run.
regions.openQuestion: Will inference demand keep pace with the chip and data center capacity now being built?

deepDives.title: Epoch AI Frontier Data Centers Hub
deepDives.why: Tracks the largest AI data centers, their power and their compute capacity.

deepDives.title: Epoch AI chip users: methodology
deepDives.why: How Epoch estimates which companies hold how much AI compute.

regions.name: Multimodal & world models
regions.summary: Video models now generate synced audio, and interactive world models generate explorable environments used for simulation and robot training.

landmarks.name: Project Genie opens to users
landmarks.summary: Google DeepMind released a prototype app built on Genie 3 that lets US AI Ultra subscribers create and explore interactive generated worlds.

landmarks.name: Waymo World Model from Genie 3
landmarks.summary: Waymo reportedly adopted a fine-tuned Genie 3 to simulate rare driving scenarios, an early industrial use of world models.
landmarks.note: Not re-checked: search budget ran out and source host was blocked in this pass.

landmarks.name: Sora 2 with synchronized audio
landmarks.summary: OpenAI's video model generates dialogue and sound with video and launched with a social app, pushing video generation to consumers.
landmarks.note: Not re-checked: search budget ran out and source host was blocked in this pass.

regions.whyItMatters: Video and world models extend AI from text to simulation, media and training data for robots.
regions.openQuestion: Do generated worlds stay consistent enough to train agents and robots that work in reality?

regions.name: Agent architectures, memory & tool use
regions.summary: Tool-use standards like MCP are now shared infrastructure under a neutral foundation. Persistent memory and continual learning for long-running agents remain open problems.

landmarks.name: Agent Skills joins Agentic AI Foundation
landmarks.summary: Anthropic donated the Agent Skills standard to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation, which it co-founded with Block and OpenAI in 2025 and which already hosts MCP.

landmarks.name: MCP 2026-07-28 spec goes stateless
landmarks.summary: The Model Context Protocol dropped its session handshake for a stateless request/response core, so any request can hit any server instance behind a load balancer.

landmarks.name: Memory-centric continual learning
landmarks.summary: Paper proposes judging agent memory by whether it improves future actions, with scaling laws for experience, storage and compute.
landmarks.note: Not re-checked: search budget ran out and source host was blocked in this pass.

regions.whyItMatters: Shared protocols and memory decide whether agents can work across tools and improve over long tasks.
regions.openQuestion: How should long-running agents store and reuse experience without retraining the underlying model?

regions.name: Embodied AI & robotics
regions.summary: Vision-language-action models now control full humanoid bodies across robot types. Factories for home humanoids have opened, but real deployments remain small.

landmarks.name: Gemini Robotics 2
landmarks.summary: Google DeepMind model with whole-body humanoid control that ran three robot embodiments from one checkpoint, including Apptronik Apollo.

landmarks.name: 1X opens NEO humanoid factory
landmarks.summary: 1X began production of its NEO home humanoid in Hayward, California, targeting 10,000 units in year one; customer delivery timing is unclear.
landmarks.note: Not re-checked: search budget ran out and source host was blocked in this pass.

landmarks.name: Physical Intelligence raises $600M
landmarks.summary: Robot foundation model startup behind the cross-embodiment pi0.5 model raised a Series B at a reported $5.6B valuation.
landmarks.note: Not re-checked: search budget ran out and source host was blocked in this pass.

regions.whyItMatters: Robotics tests whether foundation-model progress carries over to physical work.
regions.openQuestion: Can general robot models reach the reliability needed for unsupervised use in homes and factories?
